target_customer: Developers who want to embed shared browsers or remote computers in apps; consumers for the watch party app
problem: Screen sharing is single player; developers need a cloud browser that many participants can control together.
business_model: Usage-based API per participant minute ($0.007 per minute per the site) plus consumer watch party product
product_category: Virtual computer and multiplayer browser API

founders.name: Declan Goncalves
education: University of Waterloo (met cofounders there per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page; no further background listed

competitors.name: Teleparty
competitors.what: Browser extension for synced streaming watch parties (formerly Netflix Party)

competitors.name: Rabb.it
competitors.what: Shared virtual browser watch party app that shut down before Hyperbeam launched

technical_complexity.rationale: Running low-latency remote Chrome and Android sessions in the cloud with synced audio, input and many participants is hard for students.

defensibility.rationale: Streaming infrastructure is replicable by funded rivals, and later browser-agent infrastructure startups entered the space.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented; the API found a developer niche.

market_need_then: Remote watching boomed during the pandemic; Hyperbeam's blog claims 1.5 million sign-ups and 150K monthly users for the watch party product, and Rabb.it's shutdown left a gap.

branding.name_origin: Began as Tutturu.tv, a Waterloo capstone watch party site; renamed Hyperbeam (rename reason not sourced)

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and benefit-driven; tagline Vaporize the Distance

rebrands.why: Not sourced; the yespress headline says Tutturu became Hyperbeam

branding.community_and_virality: Watch party product claimed 150K monthly users; launched on Product Hunt per one aggregator.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable sci-fi name fitting a teleporting browser, but little independent press on the brand.

pivots.from: Consumer anime watch party site Tutturu
pivots.to: Hyperbeam watch party plus virtual computer API for developers
pivots.why: Per yespress headline, joined YC and opened the engine to developers; date not given

outcome_analysis: Hyperbeam grew from a Waterloo capstone watch party site into a developer API for embedded virtual computers and is still active. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding is unclear: a 2022 company blog calls it bootstrapped, while aggregators list a $500K YC note, so the capital story is unresolved. The API faces newer well-funded cloud browser startups.
notes: Funding conflict: CB Insights and standout.work list a $500K convertible note on 2022-03-30 with YC, Pioneer Fund and Waterloo endowment; the company's 2022 blog says completely bootstrapped. Aggregator only, so not recorded as a round. Competitors come from Hyperbeam's own blog (footer 2022), not a third party. yespress profile of Philip Scott returned HTTP 403. Founded year 2021 per CB Insights only.
